records.summary: The records show a significant obstacle at this address: an ABC Type 48 (bar) referral was denied by Planning in September 2022—two months ago—because Planning Code Section 202.12 requires a Conditional Use Authorization to change the use of a laundromat, even though bar use is principally permitted on the ground floor in the RC-4 zoning district. The block is densely developed with alcohol uses: 24 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft (92 within 1,000 ft) and 5 bars within 500 ft. Nearby bar approvals in RC-4 (801 Bush, 845 Bush, 895 Bush) were for continuations of existing bar uses or transfers, not new conversions requiring discretionary review.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 895 Bush St in RC-4, approved July 2014, 157 meters away. Same corridor, same zoning, same license type.
comparables.key_takeaway: This agency referral was approved within 10 days because it was for an existing bar use (Stookey's Club Moderne). The pattern on this corridor is that existing bar uses are routinely approved, while new conversions—especially from protected uses like laundromats—face discretionary review.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar (Type 42, beer/wine) at 845 Bush St in RC-4, approved January 2003, 110 meters away. Same block and zoning district.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 42 referral for a bar in RC-4, citing that bar use is permitted on the ground floor per Planning Code Sections 209.8(c)/218(b). However, as an agency referral it does not address whether a laundromat conversion would be allowed; the approval confirms the use is permitted in the abstract but does not waive Section 202.12.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 925 Bush St in RC-4, approved January 2019, 224 meters away. Transfer of existing bar use in the same zoning district.
comparables.key_takeaway: This Type 48 transfer was approved for an existing bar. The description explicitly states 'Continuation of existing use,' confirming that transfers of existing bar licenses in RC-4 are straightforward, while new bar uses replacing other uses—especially laundromats—require a CUA.

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for a restaurant and bar at 532–536 Sutter St in C-3-R, 73 meters away, filed April 2013 and withdrawn April 2015 after two years. This is the only true use-decision case (not an agency referral) among nearby bar applications in the last decade.
comparables.key_takeaway: The applicant withdrew this CUA to convert an assembly hall to a restaurant and bar after two years of processing. While the record does not state a reason, the withdrawal illustrates the time, cost and uncertainty of a discretionary hearing for a new bar use in this area. This is the path 779 Bush now faces.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 580 Sutter St in C-3-R, approved February 2022, 58 meters away. Recent approval in a nearby downtown commercial district.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 48 agency referral in three weeks because it was a continuation of an existing bar use. Even in a district where bar use is principally permitted, Planning emphasized 'Continuation of existing use,' reinforcing that new conversions—particularly from protected uses—are treated differently.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar at 801–811 Bush St in RC-4, approved February 2000, 55 meters away. Early precedent on this block showing long-standing bar use in RC-4.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a full bar in RC-4 citing Sections 209.8(c)/218(b), confirming that bar use has been principally permitted in RC-4 for over 20 years. However, this was an agency referral without detail on prior use, so it does not inform whether a laundromat conversion would have been allowed.

comparables.why_comparable: DPH referral for bar use (Stookey's Club Moderne) at 895 Bush St in RC-4, approved June 2015, 157 meters away. Same location as MB1401206, a year later.
comparables.key_takeaway: Another approval for the same existing bar at 895 Bush (Stookey's), this time as a DPH health permit referral. The consistent approvals for this established bar reinforce that the Section 202.12 laundromat-conversion obstacle at 779 Bush is unique to that site, not a general bar policy in RC-4.

patterns.pattern: All bar approvals in RC-4 on the Bush Street corridor (801, 845, 895, 925 Bush) were for continuation, transfer or expansion of existing bar uses, not new conversions from other use types. The September 2022 denial at 779 Bush is the only case where Planning blocked a bar because the prior use (laundromat) triggered Planning Code Section 202.12's mandatory CUA requirement.

Agency referrals (ABC or DPH asking Planning whether a bar use is allowed) are approved routinely—often within 10 to 30 days—when the bar use already exists or is a transfer. Continuations of existing bar uses on this corridor were approved in 10 days (MB1401206), 19 days (2022-000994MIS), 17 days (2018-016962MIS), and 21 days (MB0000122).

Planning Code Section 202.12 requires a Conditional Use Authorization for any change of use or demolition of a laundromat, regardless of whether the proposed new use is otherwise principally permitted in the zoning district. The denial at 779 Bush explicitly cited this section, and it overrides the RC-4 principal-permitted status of bar use.

The only discretionary use decision (CUA) for a bar within 1,000 feet in the last decade was withdrawn after two years (2013.0508C at 532–536 Sutter St). This illustrates the timeline and uncertainty of a CUA process for a new bar use in this area.

Bar use has been principally permitted at ground floor in RC-4 for over 20 years, per Planning Code Sections 209.3, 209.8(c) and 218(b). Multiple agency referrals cite these sections when approving bars in RC-4. However, this does not waive Section 202.12 when the prior use is a laundromat.

ABC will not issue a license when Planning recommends denial on an agency referral. The denial at 779 Bush means ABC will not process a Type 48 application until the operator obtains a CUA from the Planning Commission approving the laundromat conversion.

risk.concept_summary: A 3,580 sq ft bar without food service at 779 Bush St (RC-4 zoning), converting the existing laundromat, with tenant improvements and recorded music.

overall.next_step: Confirm with San Francisco Planning in writing whether a Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 202.12 is required to convert this laundromat to bar use, and whether the September 2022 denial can be reconsidered or requires a new CUA filing.

approvals.summary: A Conditional Use Authorization is required because Planning Code Section 202.12 mandates one for any change of use or demolition of a laundromat, even though bar use is principally permitted at ground floor in RC-4.

findings.text: An ABC Type 48 referral for a bar at this exact address was denied by Planning on 2022-09-08 because Section 202.12 requires a Conditional Use Authorization to convert a laundromat, overriding the RC-4 principal-permitted status of bar use.

Bar use is principally permitted on the ground floor in RC-4 per Planning Code Section 209.3, but Section 202.12 (in force 2021-12-20 to 2024-12-20) requires a conditional use for any change of use or demolition of a laundromat.
All nearby bar approvals in RC-4 (801 Bush Oct 2021, 845 Bush Jan 2003, 895 Bush Jul 2014) were for existing bar uses (continuation or transfer), not conversions from other use types.

The only discretionary bar application within 1,000 ft in the last decade—a CUA to convert an assembly hall to restaurant and bar at 532 Sutter St—was withdrawn after 708 days (filed April 2013, withdrawn April 2015).

approvals.summary: ABC will not issue a licence until Planning approves the laundromat conversion, but which licence type (Type 42 beer/wine or Type 48 full bar) and how it will be obtained (new application or transfer) are not given, so the timeline and process cannot be determined.

findings.text: ABC will not process a licence application when Planning recommends denial on an agency referral; the September 2022 denial means ABC will require a CUA approval before issuing any licence for this address.

The concept description does not state what alcohol will be served (beer and wine only, or full liquor) or how the licence will be obtained (new application or transfer), so the applicable ABC licence type and process are not established.

92 active on-sale ABC licences are on file within 1,000 ft of the address, and the density statistics flag undue concentration; if the census tract exceeds the county ratio for crime or licence density, ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city, adding 1–3 months.

approvals.summary: A bar serving only beverages (no food) needs a health permit to operate, issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing, which is allowed once the CUA is granted.

findings.text: A bar serving beverages needs a San Francisco Department of Public Health permit to operate, issued after plan check and final inspection confirm the facility meets California Retail Food Code requirements.
The health permit application will be referred to Planning for zoning review, which will confirm that the CUA has been granted before recommending approval.

approvals.summary: Tenant improvements and a change of use from laundromat to bar require a building permit; whether a Building Code change of occupancy is also required depends on whether the occupant load is under or over 50, which is not stated.

findings.text: Tenant improvements and a Planning Code change of use (laundromat to bar) require a building permit, and the permit must conform to the Planning Code (including the CUA) before it is issued per Planning Code Section 175.

A bar with fewer than 50 occupants is Building Code Group B; 50 or more is Assembly Group A-2. The concept description does not give the occupant load, so whether a Building Code change of occupancy is required is not established.
The existing occupancy group of the laundromat is not in public records; only an architect's review of the space or the Certificate of Occupancy on file at DBI would show it.

expected_conditions.condition: Operating hours ending by 2 a.m. (state law maximum for on-sale alcohol service).
expected_conditions.basis: California Business and Professions Code Section 25631 prohibits on-sale alcohol service between 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. statewide. The concept states it closes before midnight, which is well within the limit.

expected_conditions.condition: A good-neighbor policy addressing noise, litter, loitering and patron behavior, to be submitted with the CUA application and enforced as a condition of approval.
expected_conditions.basis: Conditional Use findings under Planning Code Section 303(c) require that the use will not be detrimental to the neighborhood. High alcohol-licence density (24 on-sale licences within 500 ft) and the laundromat-conversion issue make a good-neighbor commitment likely.

expected_conditions.condition: Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) certification for all alcohol servers and managers within 60 days of hire, and proof on site for ABC inspections.
expected_conditions.basis: California AB 1221 requires RBS certification for every server and manager in an on-sale alcohol establishment. ABC enforces it through inspections.

expected_conditions.condition: A limit on amplified sound or music volume if the Planning Commission finds it necessary to protect residential units above or nearby.
expected_conditions.basis: The concept plays recorded music, and RC-4 is a residential-commercial district with housing nearby. Noise conditions are common in bar CUAs in mixed-use districts, though no specific precedent is cited here.

expected_conditions.condition: Security or staffing plan if the bar operates past 10 p.m. or the occupant load exceeds a threshold set by the Commission.
expected_conditions.basis: Bar CUAs in areas with high foot traffic or existing nightlife often include security conditions. The high density of alcohol uses on this block and the Type 48 (public premises, no food requirement) classification make this plausible.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether a new CUA application is required or whether the September 2022 denial can be reconsidered with revised plans or operating conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that you are the new applicant for 779 Bush St and reference the September 2022 ABC referral denial (file 2022-008099MIS). Ask whether Planning will accept a new CUA application under Section 202.12 for the laundromat conversion, or whether the prior denial can be appealed or reconsidered if the concept or commitments change. Request the name of the planner who will handle the case and the current CUA application fee.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) online through the California Secretary of State bizfile portal. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) online at IRS.gov the same day; it is free and issued immediately. Use the entity name and EIN for all subsequent filings.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer and obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the bar name differs from the entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the SF Treasurer within 30 days of forming the entity. The fee is tiered by projected gross receipts ($55–$700); estimate conservatively. The BAN is required for every other city permit. If the public-facing bar name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail, then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC require the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA (required before ABC will accept a licence application).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online at the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) website. The seller's permit is free and often issued the same day. CDTFA may request a security deposit depending on projected sales. ABC will not issue an alcohol licence until the seller's permit exists, so do this immediately after forming the entity.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, operating plan, good-neighbor policy, and plans showing the bar layout and any tenant improvements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application online through the Planning Department portal with the BAN. The application fee for a bar CUA with tenant improvements is approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost; confirm the fee schedule with Planning. Attach a narrative explaining that the laundromat will be removed and the space converted to a bar, the hours of operation (state that you will close before midnight if that remains the plan), a good-neighbor commitment addressing noise, litter and patron conduct, and scaled floor plans showing the bar layout, restrooms, egress and any structural or finish work. Planning will schedule a pre-application meeting, assign the case to environmental review (likely a categorical exemption), post a notice at the site for 30 days, mail notice to properties within 300 feet, and calendar a Planning Commission hearing. Budget 4–10 months from filing to…

filing_playbook.action: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA and the 30-day appeal period expires, file the ABC licence application (Type 42 for beer/wine or Type 47/48 for full bar, depending on the concept).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: If the bar will serve beer and wine only, apply for a Type 41 (eating place, requires food) or Type 42 (public premises, no food). If full liquor, you must purchase and transfer an existing Type 47 (eating place) or Type 48 (public premises) licence, as they are quota licences unavailable new. Engage an ABC licence broker if purchasing a licence; budget $100k–$450k for a Type 47/48 in San Francisco. Submit the ABC application online with the seller's permit number, the approved CUA, a lease, and a diagram of the premises. Post the ABC public notice at the site for 30 days. ABC will refer the application to SFPD and Planning; Planning will issue a zoning sign-off citing the CUA. If the census tract shows undue concentration, Planning may require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors, adding 1–3 months. Budget 60–240 days for ABC approval and transfer, dep…

filing_playbook.action: File for a health permit to operate with the San Francisco Department of Public Health, including a menu (beverages only) and floor plan, after the CUA is approved.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online through the DPH Environmental Health portal with your BAN, Location ID (LIN) and EIN. The permit application fee is $470 (FY 2026–27), and the annual licence fee for bars is $0 for 2026–28. Attach a beverage list, floor plan showing bar, sinks, restrooms and storage, and proof that a Certified Food Protection Manager is on staff (even a bar needs one employee with the certificate). DPH will refer the application to Planning, which will confirm the CUA. Schedule a pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance with your DPH plan reviewer. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes. Budget 2–6 weeks after the CUA and plans are submitted.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application for tenant improvements and change of use with the Department of Building Inspection, routed to Planning for CUA conformance review.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the building permit application online or at the DBI permit counter with plans stamped by a licensed architect, the approved CUA, and the project description. The permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation (estimate $800–$15,000). DBI will route the application to Planning under Section 175; Planning will confirm the work conforms to the CUA. If the occupant load is 50 or more or you install a commercial hood, the Fire Department will also review. Separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed contractors. Schedule DPH and Fire inspections before the final DBI inspection. Budget 1–4 months for plan review and approval, depending on the completeness of the plans.

timeline_cost.notes: These figures are the time and government cost to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, health permit and building permit for tenant improvements—the three approvals in the entitlement path—when they are granted. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days from filing to final approval (including pre-application, environmental review, noticing, hearing and the 30-day appeal period), with a city fee of approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost. The health permit adds 14–45 days and $470 after the CUA is approved. The building permit for tenant improvements adds 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction cost) and is processed in parallel with or after the CUA. These figures do not include the ABC licence, which cannot be filed until the CUA is granted; add 60–240 days and $1,000–$1,600 for a new Type 41/42 (beer/wine), or 90–240 days and $17,000–$450,000 to purchase and transfer a Type 47/48 (full bar). The alcohol licence type and transaction method are not stated, so no ABC time or cost is included here. Also not included: entity formation, business registration, FBN, seller's permit, RBS training, workers' comp, music licences, sign permit, and any costs to remediate the laundromat or purchase a transferred liquor licence. Professional fees (architect, expediter, ABC broker, lawyer) are not government costs and are not included.
